neighbours.label: predicts an upcoming fight or quarrel noun: the article after 'the two X got into a ▁' or 'had a ▁' between two parties, and the first piece of the conflict noun itself (quar-, falling (out), раз-ногласий); fires on 'got into a' even when a taxi follows
fire: Two of the defenders got into a shoving match in the car park after the final whistle.
The brothers had a bitter quarrel over the will and never spoke again.
Her parents got into a screaming row every Christmas about whose turn it was to carve.
The partnership ended after a falling out over the direction of the company.
Two drunk fans got into a brawl outside the stadium and were held overnight.
The composer and his librettist had a furious dispute about the final act.
Из-за разногласий с продюсером режиссёр покинул проект в середине съёмок.
The cousins got into a fistfight at the wedding and the police were called.
quiet: Two of the defenders stayed in the car park signing shirts after the final whistle.
The brothers read the will together and divided the furniture in an afternoon.
Her parents cooked an enormous dinner every Christmas and fell asleep by the fire.
The partnership grew after a decision to move the company to Leeds.
Two cheerful fans sang outside the stadium and were filmed for the news.
The composer and his librettist shared a long lunch to celebrate the final act.
После долгих переговоров с продюсером режиссёр подписал контракт в середине лета.
The cousins danced at the wedding until the band packed up at midnight.

predictions: 8/8 fire at 0.5-0.9; near misses without the two-party conflict setup under 0.25
notes: Probe: 'the two players got into a fist fight' 0.908 at ' a' and 'got into a taxi' also 0.908 at ' a' (a predictor, blind to the noun); 'got into a heated argument' 0.795; 'had a quarrel' 0.623 at ' quar'; 'falling outs' 0.578; разногласий 0.525 at ' раз'. 'had a barbecue' 0.353, 'broke up after years of touring' 0.218, library floor 0.016. Near misses therefore avoid 'got into a' and 'had a' after two parties rather than only swapping the noun. The + pole suppresses 'fight', 'quarrel', 'argument'.
